pages.reference/cli-parity: Candle's commands in the Candle Harness

features.name: What the Candle Harness is
features.what: A trading terminal for Candle with an AI agent beside you, run on your own Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode or Pi. One local core holds the keys and state; every view and agent attaches to it, and every trade the agent proposes is a card you approve, unless you've let its wallet trade inside limits.

features.name: Opening the Candle Harness
features.what: candle tui or candle-harness opens the view, starting the core if none is running.

features.name: Setup
features.what: With no agent yet, the Candle Harness opens on setup: sign in to Candle, connect your agent's engine, a vault or the embedded wallet only, the agent's key with Candle's cap, its wallet, limits and approvals, then funds or paper. A run that stops picks up where it was. candle-harness setup runs it again to add an agent.

features.name: Funding a wallet
features.what: Setup shows the wallet's address with a copy chip, and moves on once a deposit lands. Paper needs no funds.

features.name: The tour
features.what: About a minute over the real screen: the agent, positions, a card, the kill switch, settings ▾ and the palette. Setup's last step opens it, and the palette's "the tour" runs it again.

features.name: Where to start
features.what: Trade or the Cockpit, picked at the end of setup and kept as the tab the Candle Harness opens on.

features.name: Paper and live
features.what: Paper trades are recorded at the quoted price and never sent; live trades move real funds. Switching to live asks first, and the mode last picked survives a restart.

features.name: The status bar
features.what: Along the top: the mode, the active agent, the P&L figure with its window, and the kill switch's chip.

features.name: Tabs
features.what: Each tab shows a saved layout. Click one, or press its digit from the tab bar. On a narrow terminal the names shrink before settings ▾ is cut.

features.name: Panes and focus
features.what: Tab and the arrows move focus between panes. ↑/↓ in a list moves a highlight, and the highlighted row's token is linked once it rests.

features.name: Scrolling
features.what: Every pane scrolls with PgUp/PgDn or the wheel, and its bottom border says what's out of view.

features.name: The palette
features.what: ctrl-k lists every action, tab, layout, pane, agent, preset, memory, token, alias, theme and Candle command, and typing searches them all. A pick does what its key or click does; it never approves a card or quits. Its settings row opens the settings menu by keys.

features.name: The input line
features.what: Type a command or a message and press Enter. The hint line beside it says what Enter and Esc do here. Esc twice clears a typed line.

features.name: Help
features.what: ? with the line empty lists the commands you can type and every key; c from there opens the palette at Candle's commands.

features.name: Quitting
features.what: ctrl-c twice quits. Once clears the line, closes what's open, or copies text selected with the mouse.

features.name: The mouse and copying
features.what: Chips, cards, rows and tabs take clicks. ⧉ copies an address in full, and text selected with the mouse copies with ctrl-c.

features.name: settings ▾
features.what: Beside the tabs: which tabs show, each tab's layout, the theme, your agent's model and memory, skill folders, aliases, the P&L window, approvals, triggers, bots and the vault.

features.name: Small terminals
features.what: Below a layout's width it collapses into the agent and one switched pane.

features.name: Empty panes
features.what: Every pane says what it will show before its first read, and why when a read fails.

features.name: Your agent's engine
features.what: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode or Pi: your own install and sign-in, run in a private home each turn with your own setup kept out. The Candle Harness ships no model login of its own.

features.name: The model picker
features.what: ctrl-g or the agent pane's chip lists each engine with its version, sign-in, gaps and models, searchable. A pick runs from the next turn, for that agent, and is kept across restarts.

features.name: Presets
features.what: Quant, the default, works as an analyst on Hacc's data with Candle's skills. Trader is a plain trading agent, and Bare carries the essentials only. Each agent has its own.

features.name: Skills
features.what: Quant reads ten of Candle's own skills, built in. Any preset reads skills of yours in the skills folder beside config.toml.

features.name: Your skill folders
features.what: settings ▾ → skills turns on your Claude Code, Codex and other skill folders. The core reads them and serves them to the agent, which can't read them itself. They're off until you turn them on.

features.name: Memory
features.what: Each agent keeps its own memory, an index and files in its research folder, read fresh into every turn on any engine. The memory overlay pins a line so the agent keeps it through every merge, deletes any line or file, or clears it all.

features.name: The agent's history
features.what: The agent reads its own past turns, cards and paper trades, further back than its conversation, and what happened since your last session.

features.name: The research folder
features.what: The agent's own files live in its research folder. Reads outside it are refused, through links too.

features.name: Shell and tools
features.what: The shell is off by default, a list of commands, or everything, for each agent. allow and deny list tools, and a denied tool is hidden from the agent.

features.name: The code runner
features.what: Off until you turn it on for an agent, from ctrl-g's code runner row or the palette, or with a list of programs in config. Then the agent runs a script with python3, bun or node in its research folder to compute, chart or analyse from its notes, and reads the output. The system holds every run there: it reads and writes only the research folder, has no network, and stops after 60 seconds. It works on every engine, on macOS and on Linux 6.12 or later; where the system can't hold it, it isn't offered and the doctor says why. Each run shows in Activity and the Journal with its command.

features.name: The step cap
features.what: A turn stops after 30 steps, or the number set.

features.name: Several agents
features.what: Up to 12 agents, each with its own key, limits, engine, preset and memory. agent <name> makes one active, as <agent> runs one line as another, and ctrl-f shows positions, wallets and activity for every agent or the active one.

features.name: Asking the agent
features.what: Anything that isn't a command goes to the agent. It acts when you message it, not on its own. ctrl-t on a row puts a question about it on the line.
typed: what's moving on Solana right now?

features.name: Stopping a turn
features.what: Esc with the line empty stops the agent's turn; a message waiting runs next.

features.name: Replies
features.what: Replies render as Markdown, with addresses shortened and a ⧉ to copy each in full. An address the agent wrote from memory is caught and asked again.

features.name: Marks on figures
features.what: A price, market cap, liquidity, volume or balance the agent states that no tool showed this turn is dimmed with a ? after it.

features.name: What the agent is told
features.what: Each turn opens with what went through the Candle Harness since the last: trades and how they ended, cards, the kill switch, the token you picked, and what runs without asking.

features.name: Market data from Hacc
features.what: Signals, tokens, markets, wallets and social reads from Hacc, offered by your plan. Each answer is kept short and says what it left out.

features.name: Follows and rules
features.what: On Pro and Max: follows, groups and rules on Hacc. Adds happen at once with an undo; removals and a rule's add are one-press cards.

features.name: The strategy lab
features.what: On Max: save, backtest and replay a strategy.

features.name: Candle's commands through the agent
features.what: The agent can ask for any Candle CLI command, under the same rule as when you type it.

features.name: Typed trades
features.what: buy, sell and swap on the input line, in an amount, dollars or a percent. A token is a mint, or a name shown this session; a name nobody has shown is never guessed.

features.name: Cards
features.what: A trade the agent proposes is a card, priced fresh and checked against limits. Enter with the line empty approves it once it has shown for 300 ms (1.5 s when it arrived while another card was waiting), and a click does too. ctrl-n rejects, ctrl-o shows everything it's bound to, and ctrl-r re-quotes an expired one.

features.name: Typed trades without a card
features.what: A typed live trade is a card by default, or runs at once when typedTrades is instant.

features.name: How a card is priced
features.what: A card is valued fresh from Candle's market read when it's proposed, never on approve, or from Candle's quote for the exact trade once Candle offers one. Candle fills at its own price, within its slippage limit.

features.name: A trade Candle didn't answer
features.what: Read back and never sent twice. resend or abandon it, or click it in the agent pane.

features.name: Aliases
features.what: config.toml's [aliases]: b5 = "buy $5 of" makes b5 MOON buy $5 of MOON.

features.name: Chains
features.what: Up to 5 trades or candle commands split by ;. Each is checked before anything is sent, then they run one after another; one that fails stops the rest.

features.name: Candle's commands
features.what: candle <command> runs any Candle CLI command under its rule: reads at once, the rest as cards or in the prompt pane.

features.name: Launches, staking, claims, profile and posts
features.what: One-press cards like a trade's. A launch or stake is dry-run first and the card shows the preview; a public action says so on the card.

features.name: Perps: closing and protecting
features.what: With perps.writes on, closing a position, cancelling an order, take-profit and stop-loss, the cancel-all timer and flatten are one-press cards from the EVM TEE wallet. Turning the key's reduce-only on runs at once. Off, they're held.

features.name: On Candle, not in the Candle Harness yet
features.what: Limit and stop orders, Telegram alerts, and perps orders that open or add to a position, or move funds in or out.

features.name: The embedded wallet
features.what: Your account's own wallet, which each agent pays from once you've allowed it.

features.name: TEE wallets
features.what: A wallet of its own for an agent, on Pro or Max, made in the prompt pane from a vault key, on Solana or on Hood (add a Hood wallet). Its trades run through your own candle CLI with the agent's key. Stopping one is final, and it stays on the Wallets pane until it's swept home.

features.name: Which wallet pays
features.what: from <wallet> names the wallet that pays, by name or address; else the agent's default; else the embedded wallet. The card always names it.

features.name: The Wallets pane
features.what: Each wallet, its agents and its balance. Which wallets show is a setting: the active ones, all, a group, or a list.

features.name: Wallet names
features.what: One name for each wallet, kept where it's owned: Candle's label, the vault's, or the Candle Harness's own in wallets.toml. Several can be renamed as one batch.

features.name: Wallet groups
features.what: Groups by a name prefix, a list, or both, to find and fold many wallets. A group organises; it never pays.

features.name: Empty token accounts
features.what: The Wallets pane names a TEE wallet's empty token accounts and the SOL closing them returns; close takes it back.

features.name: The vault
features.what: The vault on this machine signs owner steps and funds out. It's optional: the embedded wallet trades without one, and one can be made later from settings ▾.

features.name: Each agent's limits
features.what: A per-trade and a per-day limit for each agent, checked by the core before a card is made.

features.name: Candle's caps
features.what: Candle's own caps on each key, its loss limits and its circuit breaker. A key Candle refused for its cap is held until it resets, and sells still go.

features.name: Trading inside limits
features.what: settings ▾ → approvals: each wallet asks every time, or trades inside two figures with no card and a receipt in its place. Over a figure it's a card that says which. The agent can narrow it, never widen it.

features.name: The kill switch
features.what: ctrl-x twice, kill, or the status bar's chip: buys pause, the agent stops, buy and swap cards are withdrawn, and each open sell gets a fresh card. A report says what it did. resume turns buys back on.

features.name: Agent keys
features.what: Each agent's key is stored privately for the Candle Harness, read from stdin and never an argument, and never reaches the agent or the screen. The doctor names any key with Withdraw access.

features.name: The prompt pane
features.what: Owner steps, and anything that asks for a passphrase or shows a secret, run in a pane of their own, as you. Nothing typed there reaches the core, the agent or the journal. ctrl-] leaves it behind a chip.

features.name: Funds out
features.what: Run in the prompt pane from your vault. The agent can propose one only when your own message names where and how much. An address that looks like one of yours but isn't is refused, and a new one shows amber.

features.name: What the agent never sees
features.what: Keys, passphrases, the prompt pane, and files outside its research folder.

features.name: What leaves your machine
features.what: Your conversation goes to your own model provider, trades and reads to Candle, and signal reads to Hacc.

features.name: Trade
features.what: The agent with its cards, beside the token, positions, wallets and activity.

features.name: The token pane
features.what: The linked token: its price, a chart in two-minute candles from Hacc's history, its check, and where it launched.

features.name: Cockpit
features.what: Candle's On Fire list over Signals, the token beside them, positions and activity below, and the agent down the right.

features.name: Trending
features.what: Candle's lists side by side: New, Graduated, On Fire and Final Stretch, read every 15 seconds while on screen.

features.name: Signals
features.what: Hacc's tape or your own rules' signals, in the Candle Harness's words, filtered by pattern and chain, with a pause that counts what arrives.

features.name: P&L
features.what: Candle's books for your agents, the chart over time, positions and trades. Every figure names its window: 24 hours by default, since midnight, since a time, or since last session.

features.name: Research
features.what: One token in depth: its whole check, top traders, its own signals and posts about it, beside a list to pick from.

features.name: Journal
features.what: Everything the core recorded, in words, newest first, searched over the whole file.

features.name: Perps
features.what: What works for perps today, with questions to ask the agent.

features.name: The short agent pane
features.what: Across the foot of the tabs without the agent: questions are answered there, and a waiting card keeps its place.

features.name: What your plan gives you
features.what: Free, Pro and Max: TEE wallets, Hacc's follows and the strategy lab, Research's reads, and 30, 300 or 600 requests a minute for each key.

features.name: Candle's request limit
features.what: Background reads use at most half of each key's limit and say when they slow down. A trade or a turn never waits for them.

features.name: Layouts
features.what: layouts.toml holds your tabs and layouts of your own. The layout menu opens, closes, moves and resizes panes, a dragged border resizes, and a change stays on its tab until you save it as a layout.

features.name: Which tabs show
features.what: Each tab is ticked on or off in settings ▾, and a tab ticked off keeps its layout.

features.name: Linked panes and pins
features.what: One linked token runs through every pane: the agent moves it by showing a token, and you by picking one. A pin holds a tab's token pane on its token; up to three.

features.name: Token panes side by side
features.what: A layout holds up to three token panes to compare tokens: the first follows the link, and each one you open beside it is pinned on the token shown. Their pins count among the three.

features.name: Pop-out
features.what: ctrl-p moves the focused pane into a tmux or cmux split of its own, attached to the same core; elsewhere it gives the command to copy. A popped view approves nothing, and the pane comes back when it closes.

features.name: Themes
features.what: Candle dark, Candle light, Terminal (your terminal's own colours), and your own in the themes folder, naming only what they change. Each is checked for contrast when it loads.

features.name: The agent changes the view
features.what: Ask the agent to switch tabs, build a layout (a preview you keep with a click), add a tab, filter Signals, search the Journal or make a theme, each with an undo.

features.name: While you were away
features.what: After ten minutes or more away, a note at the top of the agent pane says what happened: trades with and without a card, P&L since you left, fills outside the Candle Harness, and your signals. show all opens every section.

features.name: Triggers
features.what: When something happens (a price, a market cap, a Hacc signal, a schedule or a time once, a fill), do something: a trade through the wallet's figures, a notification, or waking an agent. The agent writes each one with you and proposes it as a card that says whether it runs on its own or asks you each time; your press saves it. The Triggers overlay, from settings ▾, the palette or the status bar's ⚡ chip, switches one off or on, removes it, or runs its expired card again; the Triggers pane shows them in a layout of your own. Pro and Max.

features.name: Rules bots
features.what: A Hacc strategy definition the Candle Harness runs for you: it enters on Hacc's tape and sells by its exits, from the wallet and agent it was approved with, on paper or live. The agent writes each one with you and proposes it as a card; your press saves it, and only your press widens one or takes it live. Pausing one stops new entries while its exits still sell; stopping one trades nothing and leaves its positions to you. A narrower bot (a smaller stake, a tighter stop, stricter filters) takes at once. Pro and Max.

features.name: Code bots
features.what: A program of yours, in a folder of yours, that trades through the Candle Harness with a token of its own, never its agent's key. Its card shows its folder and command, the wallet it pays from, paper or live, and the figures it's held to whatever its code does: a trade's, a day's, and how many positions it may hold at once. Your press saves it; editing its code needs none. Lowering a figure takes at once; raising one, going live, or another wallet, folder or command is a new card. Pro and Max.

features.name: Running code bots
features.what: The Candle Harness runs each code bot you approved: its command in its folder, with a clean environment and its token. It's restarted after a crash, after 2 seconds and then longer, up to a minute; after five crashes in ten minutes it stops trying and tells you. Its output is kept, the last 5 MB, with any key or token taken out, and its memory and CPU are checked once a minute. It stops with the core and starts again with it. `candle-harness bots` lists your bots, starts, stops and restarts a code bot's process (stopping its process leaves the bot on, so the exits the core holds still run), prints its log, and writes its token to a file in its folder, readable by you alone, for a bot you run some other way.

features.name: Building bots with your own harness
features.what: A bots folder of your own, ~/candle-bots unless you pick another, holds each code bot in a folder of its own. The Candle Harness writes AGENTS.md there with the rules every bot runs under, the client a bot trades through, and Candle's bot-building skills where coding harnesses read them; a file you change is never written over. `candle-harness bots init` writes it. In the Build tab, your own coding harness runs `candle-harness build` to read every bot's book, a bot's log and its agent's record, to test a bot's code once on paper (never live, over within 30 minutes), and to propose a bot as a card for you to approve.

features.name: The Build tab
features.what: Your own coding harness (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode, Pi, or a command of yours), unmodified and signed in as you, in a terminal pane in your bots folder, with the bots folder and the paper test running beside it. The first time, the pane asks where your bots live and which harness, writes the folder, then starts it. Every key is the harness's while the pane has focus, but ctrl-] leaves it and ctrl-x twice is still the kill switch; a click goes back in. It keeps running when you switch tabs, and ⏎ starts it again after it exits. A bot it proposes opens whole over the frame: ⏎ approves it, Esc goes back to the harness and the card waits. Proposed while you're typing in the harness, it opens without the keys, and ctrl-] or a click moves to it. A daemon a harness leaves behind is listed with a stop chip, never stopped unasked. Below 100 columns the folder and the test run fold into a strip under the harness. On Free, the harness and the folder still work; testing or proposing a bot needs Pro or Max.

features.name: The Bots tab
features.what: Your bots on the left, the one you pick on the right: its words, paper or live, each open position on a line from its stop to its target with its entry, its trailing level once armed and the price now, its book from its own fills, the backtest of its exact definition, what it skipped and its newest fills. Its chips pause it, put it back on as you approved it, stop it, flatten it (asking once), remove it, or put a change for the agent on the input line. The status bar's chip, settings ▾ and the palette open it; with no tab showing it, the same list opens over the frame.

features.name: Triggers keep running
features.what: A trigger that's on keeps the core running after you quit, and the status bar says how many are on. candle-harness stop ends the core and says what it stopped. On a Mac, keep-awake keeps it from sleeping while a trigger or bot is on.

features.name: The core at login, and on a VPS
features.what: candle-harness service install starts the core when you log in and restarts it after a crash, so triggers run with no terminal open: a LaunchAgent on a Mac, a systemd user service on Linux. On a VPS, run the Candle Harness in tmux over SSH, install the service, and switch lingering on so the core outlives your login. uninstall and status sit beside it.

features.name: From outside the Candle Harness
features.what: From a script or another terminal, as the same user, while a core runs. candle-harness ask sends an agent your message, as if typed in the Candle Harness, and prints its reply; a card it proposes still waits for your press in the Candle Harness, and the conversation, Activity and the Journal mark it from outside; --json prints the reply, how the turn ended and the cards it left as one JSON object. candle-harness cards lists the cards the Candle Harness holds and how each ended, and --wait waits for the press or the expiry; it only reads, and never approves a card. candle-harness trigger fires an on call trigger by its name, with its cooldown, its wallet's figures and the kill switch, and prints what it did. None starts a core.

features.name: Notifications
features.what: While the Candle Harness's window isn't in front, it tells you what happened: a card waiting that you didn't make, a trigger firing, a wake skipped at its cap, the kill switch, Candle holding a key, and the core stopping when nobody asked. Your computer's own notification here, the terminal's over SSH, or the bell. With no Candle Harness window open, the core sends your computer's own, on a Mac or a Linux desktop; on a VPS nothing reaches you until you reattach.

features.name: What each engine can do
features.what: Where the five engines differ: file reads, shell lists, web tools, sign-ins held back, and the model each names.

features.name: The scorecard
features.what: A set of short agent conversations against stand-in Candle and Hacc servers, scored from what the core recorded, run on each engine.

features.name: Installing
features.what: One line installs candle-harness beside Candle's CLI, checking the checksum and signature first. With no CLI, it offers to install Candle's too.

features.name: The version
features.what: candle-harness version prints the version and the commit it was built from.

features.name: The Candle Harness and Candle's CLI
features.what: The Candle Harness runs your own candle CLI as the profile setup signed in, and Candle's MCP server for each agent key.

features.name: The doctor
features.what: candle-harness doctor checks the setup and says exactly what to fix. --offline skips Candle and the engines' turns.

features.name: The debug switch
features.what: A debug switch that's on is named by the doctor, the status bar and the journal.

features.name: The core
features.what: One core for each account on this machine holds the keys and state and signs. Every view and engine attaches to it over a private socket. candle-harness core runs it headless, and candle-harness mcp is the server an engine reaches it through.

features.name: The attach protocol
features.what: The socket protocol views and engines use: requests, topics and events.

features.name: The bot protocol
features.what: How a code bot talks to the core with its own token: its trades by request id, the exits the core holds, its book and reads, what it's told and what it says, and the TypeScript client that speaks it.
